title: Session 1: Full Stack Development & MERN Stack Fundamentals

questions.questionText: What does full stack development primarily involve?
options: Creation of complete Web applications spanning all architectural layers, from front-end to back-end
questions.correctAnswer: Creation of complete Web applications spanning all architectural layers, from front-end to back-end
questions.explanation: Full stack development involves the creation of complete Web applications spanning all architectural layers, from front-end to back-end.

questions.questionText: A full stack developer is best described as someone who:
options: Is proficient in both client-side and server-side aspects of an application
questions.correctAnswer: Is proficient in both client-side and server-side aspects of an application
questions.explanation: A full stack developer is proficient in both client-side and server-side aspects of an application.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT listed as one of the primary components of full stack development?
questions.explanation: The primary components of full stack development include front-end, back-end, database management, server administration/deployment, and version control.

questions.questionText: Front-end development is primarily concerned with:
options: The user interface and user experience of a Web application
questions.correctAnswer: The user interface and user experience of a Web application
questions.explanation: Front-end development is primarily concerned with the user interface and user experience of a Web application.

questions.questionText: Which technologies form the foundation for building visual elements and interactivity on the front end?
questions.explanation: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript form the foundational technologies for building visual elements and interactivity on the front end.

questions.questionText: Back-end development is mainly responsible for:
options: Application functionality, database administration, and server-side logic
questions.correctAnswer: Application functionality, database administration, and server-side logic
questions.explanation: Back-end development is responsible for application functionality, database administration, and server-side logic.

questions.questionText: Which of the following are examples of server-side programming languages used in back-end development?
options: Node.js, Python, Ruby, Java, or PHP
questions.correctAnswer: Node.js, Python, Ruby, Java, or PHP
questions.explanation: Node.js, Python, Ruby, Java, and PHP are examples of server-side programming languages.

questions.questionText: Back-end developers provide APIs primarily to:
options: Enable data exchange and communication between front-end and back-end
Host the application on a server
questions.correctAnswer: Enable data exchange and communication between front-end and back-end
questions.explanation: APIs enable seamless data exchange and communication between the front-end and back-end.

questions.questionText: APIs stand for:
questions.explanation: API stands for Application Programming Interface.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of a relational database?
questions.explanation: MySQL is a well-known example of a relational database management system.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of a NoSQL database?
questions.explanation: MongoDB is a leading example of a NoSQL document database.

questions.questionText: The choice between relational and NoSQL databases in full-stack development typically depends on:
options: The price of the software license
questions.explanation: The choice between relational and NoSQL databases depends primarily on the application's data structure and scalability requirements.

questions.questionText: What is the primary role of a Web server?
options: To handle client requests, process them, and return results to users
questions.correctAnswer: To handle client requests, process them, and return results to users
questions.explanation: A web server's primary role is to handle client requests, process them according to business logic, and return results to users.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a tool used to build and manage Web servers?
questions.explanation: Express.js, Django, and Flask are server frameworks, while Photoshop is graphic design software.

questions.questionText: To make a Web application available to users, full-stack developers must:
options: Deploy it to a Web server or cloud platform
questions.correctAnswer: Deploy it to a Web server or cloud platform
questions.explanation: Full-stack developers must deploy applications to a web server or cloud platform to make them publicly available to users.

questions.questionText: Knowledge of server administration and deployment procedures is important because it:
options: Improves the color scheme of the website
Removes the need for a database
questions.explanation: Server administration and deployment knowledge ensures efficient, reliable, and secure application hosting.

questions.questionText: Which tool is cited as a crucial version control system for full-stack engineers?
questions.explanation: Git is the crucial version control system used by full-stack engineers to track changes and collaborate.

questions.questionText: What does the acronym MERN stand for?
questions.explanation: MERN stands for MongoDB, Express, ReactJS, and Node.js.

questions.questionText: In the MERN stack, which technology serves as the NoSQL database?
questions.explanation: MongoDB serves as the NoSQL document database in the MERN stack.

questions.questionText: In the MERN stack, which technology handles the front-end of the application?
questions.explanation: ReactJS is the client-side library responsible for the front-end user interface in the MERN stack.

questions.questionText: In the MERN stack, which component acts as the server-side runtime environment?
questions.explanation: Node.js is the JavaScript runtime environment executing code on the server side.

questions.questionText: In the MERN stack, which technology is a minimal and flexible Web application framework used to build APIs and server-side functionality?
questions.explanation: Express is a minimal and flexible web application framework for Node.js used to build APIs and back-end functionality.

questions.questionText: Which company is responsible for the development and upkeep of ReactJS?
questions.explanation: Facebook (now Meta) developed and maintains ReactJS.

questions.questionText: In what year was ReactJS initially released?
questions.explanation: ReactJS was originally created by Jordan Walke and open-sourced by Facebook in 2013.

questions.questionText: ReactJS is particularly renowned for its ability to construct:
questions.explanation: ReactJS is famous for constructing dynamic user interfaces and Single Page Applications (SPAs).

questions.questionText: React allows developers to build interfaces using reusable code fragments called:
questions.explanation: React uses reusable, encapsulated code units called components to build complex user interfaces.

questions.questionText: What does JSX stand for in the context of ReactJS?
questions.explanation: JSX stands for JavaScript XML, allowing HTML-like syntax inside JavaScript.

questions.questionText: JSX enables developers to:
options: Embed HTML-like code within their JavaScript components
Connect directly to a database without an API
questions.correctAnswer: Embed HTML-like code within their JavaScript components
questions.explanation: JSX allows developers to write and embed HTML-like structures directly inside JavaScript components.

questions.questionText: What is the Virtual DOM in ReactJS?
options: A physical server used to host React apps
A lightweight, in-memory representation of the actual DOM used to optimize UI updates
A database used to store UI state
questions.correctAnswer: A lightweight, in-memory representation of the actual DOM used to optimize UI updates
questions.explanation: The Virtual DOM is an in-memory representation of real DOM elements, used by React to compute efficient diffs.

questions.questionText: How does the Virtual DOM improve performance in ReactJS?
options: By storing data permanently in the database
By comparing the Virtual DOM with the real DOM and applying only essential updates
By eliminating the need for JavaScript
questions.correctAnswer: By comparing the Virtual DOM with the real DOM and applying only essential updates
questions.explanation: React compares the Virtual DOM tree with the previous one and reconciles only the changed nodes in the real DOM.

questions.questionText: React's Unidirectional Data Flow means that:
options: Data moves in one direction, from parent to child components
Data moves in one direction, from child to parent components
Data cannot move between components at all
questions.correctAnswer: Data moves in one direction, from parent to child components
questions.explanation: Unidirectional data flow means data always flows downwards from parent components to child components via props.

questions.questionText: Which of the following can be combined with ReactJS to handle global application state in complex applications?
questions.explanation: Redux and the React Context API are standard solutions for managing global application state in React applications.

questions.questionText: Node.js is best described as:
questions.explanation: Node.js is an open-source, cross-platform JavaScript runtime environment that executes JavaScript code outside a web browser.

questions.questionText: Which JavaScript engine does Node.js rely on?
questions.explanation: Node.js is built on Google Chrome's V8 JavaScript engine.

questions.questionText: One of Node.js's key strengths is its:
questions.explanation: Node.js uses an event-driven, non-blocking I/O model that makes it lightweight and efficient.

questions.questionText: Node.js's ecosystem of modules and packages is managed through:
questions.explanation: NPM (Node Package Manager) is the default package manager for Node.js, providing access to hundreds of thousands of reusable packages.

questions.questionText: Node.js's cross-platform capability means it can run on:
questions.explanation: Node.js runs across Windows, macOS, and Linux operating systems.

questions.questionText: Node.js is often the preferred choice for building which type of applications?
options: Collaborative tools, gaming servers, and chat applications
questions.correctAnswer: Collaborative tools, gaming servers, and chat applications
questions.explanation: Due to its asynchronous event-driven nature, Node.js excels at real-time collaborative tools, gaming servers, and chat applications.

questions.questionText: Why can developers use the same language for both front-end and back-end development in a MERN-type stack?
options: Because Node.js allows JavaScript to run on the server side
Because Express replaces JavaScript with Java
Because ReactJS runs only on the server
questions.correctAnswer: Because Node.js allows JavaScript to run on the server side
questions.explanation: Node.js allows JavaScript to execute on the server, enabling full-stack development using a single programming language across both client and server.

questions.questionText: Express is best described as:
options: A fast, minimal, and flexible Node.js Web application framework
questions.correctAnswer: A fast, minimal, and flexible Node.js Web application framework
questions.explanation: Express is a fast, unopinionated, minimalist web application framework for Node.js.

questions.questionText: Express simplifies the task of building which of the following?
options: APIs, Web servers, and other back-end functionalities
questions.correctAnswer: APIs, Web servers, and other back-end functionalities
questions.explanation: Express provides a robust set of features to develop web and mobile applications, APIs, and web servers.

questions.questionText: In Express, functions that execute before or after processing a request are called:
questions.explanation: Middleware functions in Express have access to the request object (req), response object (res), and the next middleware function in the application's request-response cycle.

questions.questionText: What is the main benefit of Express middleware?
options: It removes the need for routing
It simplifies code organization and facilitates the use of third-party functionality
It replaces the need for a database
It prevents the use of APIs
questions.correctAnswer: It simplifies code organization and facilitates the use of third-party functionality
questions.explanation: Middleware enhances code modularity and allows easy integration of third-party capabilities like logging, body parsing, and authentication.

questions.questionText: In Express, routing involves developers defining URL paths and associating them with specific:
options: HTTP methods such as GET, POST, PUT, DELETE
questions.correctAnswer: HTTP methods such as GET, POST, PUT, DELETE
questions.explanation: Routing refers to determining how an application responds to a client request to a particular endpoint with a specific HTTP method (GET, POST, etc.).

questions.questionText: Which of the following are examples of template engines used with Express for dynamic server-side HTML rendering?
questions.explanation: EJS, Pug, and Handlebars are popular template engines used with Express to generate dynamic HTML pages on the server.

questions.questionText: Express's popularity among Node.js developers for building Web applications and RESTful APIs largely stems from its:
options: Extensive and active community, comprehensive documentation, and wide array of plugins
Requirement to use only one database
questions.correctAnswer: Extensive and active community, comprehensive documentation, and wide array of plugins
questions.explanation: Express is widely adopted due to its vibrant community, rich ecosystem of plugins, and comprehensive documentation.

questions.questionText: MongoDB is best described as:
options: An open-source NoSQL database purpose-built for unstructured and semi-structured data
questions.correctAnswer: An open-source NoSQL database purpose-built for unstructured and semi-structured data
questions.explanation: MongoDB is an open-source NoSQL document database designed to handle unstructured and semi-structured data with high flexibility.

questions.questionText: In MongoDB, data is organized into documents that resemble:
questions.explanation: MongoDB stores data records as BSON (binary JSON) documents, which resemble standard JSON objects.

questions.questionText: What does "schema-free" (schema-less) mean in the context of MongoDB?
options: Data must follow a rigid, predefined structure
Fields can vary among documents within the same collection, offering flexible data modeling
Every document must have identical fields
questions.correctAnswer: Fields can vary among documents within the same collection, offering flexible data modeling
questions.explanation: Schema-less means documents in the same collection do not need to possess identical sets of fields, allowing adaptable and evolving data models.

questions.questionText: What are "ad hoc queries" in MongoDB?
options: Queries that require predefined schemas or joins
Dynamic and complex searches on data that eliminate the need for predefined schemas or joins
Queries that only work with relational databases
questions.correctAnswer: Dynamic and complex searches on data that eliminate the need for predefined schemas or joins
questions.explanation: MongoDB supports ad hoc queries, allowing developers to query by field, range queries, and regular expression searches dynamically.

questions.questionText: MongoDB achieves horizontal scaling across multiple servers or nodes through a process called:
questions.explanation: Sharding is the method MongoDB uses to distribute data across multiple machines to support deployments with very large datasets and high throughput operations.

questions.questionText: Which MongoDB feature enhances the speed and efficiency of query operations on large datasets?
questions.explanation: Indexes support the efficient execution of queries in MongoDB by preventing full collection scans.

questions.questionText: MongoDB's Aggregation Framework is primarily used for:
questions.explanation: The Aggregation Framework allows developers to process data records and return computed results via multistage pipelines.

questions.questionText: Automatic failover and replication in MongoDB primarily ensure:
options: High availability and data redundancy in the event of server failures
questions.correctAnswer: High availability and data redundancy in the event of server failures
questions.explanation: MongoDB replica sets provide redundancy and high availability through automatic failover if the primary node becomes unavailable.

questions.questionText: Which MongoDB feature is specifically designed for efficiently storing and retrieving large files such as images, videos, and audio?
questions.explanation: GridFS is a specification for storing and retrieving files that exceed the BSON-document size limit of 16 MB by dividing files into chunks.

questions.questionText: MongoDB's support for geospatial indexing and queries makes it particularly well-suited for:
options: Applications that don't require a database
questions.explanation: Geospatial queries and 2dsphere indexes enable location-aware features such as finding nearby places and calculating distances.

questions.questionText: In the three-tier MongoDB architecture, which layer houses the actual data, typically hosted in MongoDB Atlas?
questions.explanation: The Data Layer (Database Tier) is where data is persistently stored and managed, often on MongoDB Atlas.

questions.questionText: Which layer in the MongoDB three-tier architecture interacts with the database and typically corresponds to the API, often built using Node.js?
questions.explanation: The Application Layer contains the business logic and API endpoints (built with Node.js/Express) that communicate with the database.

questions.questionText: The Presentation Layer in the three-tier architecture corresponds to:
options: The JavaScript front-end (e.g. React or Angular) where users interact with the application UI
questions.correctAnswer: The JavaScript front-end (e.g. React or Angular) where users interact with the application UI
questions.explanation: The Presentation Layer is the client-facing UI (built with React, Angular, etc.) through which users interact with the application.

questions.questionText: In the three-tier MongoDB architecture diagram, which component connects the back-end server to the database?
options: MongoDB Drivers within the Application Layer
questions.correctAnswer: MongoDB Drivers within the Application Layer
questions.explanation: MongoDB Drivers (such as the Node.js MongoDB driver or Mongoose) within the Application Layer provide the connection and communication channel between the application server and the database.
